To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
claudin-3 and claudin-4 are expressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and polyps, and that the expression of claudin is associated with the histological differentiation and the tumor stage.

(1) the expression of all claudins was increased in CRC compared with the normal mucosa, with the highest expression in adenomas; (2) claudin-3 expression was the most significant predictor for CRC and adenoma; and (3) claudin expression was associated with the tumor stage.

(1) the expression of claudins 1, 3 and 4 in normal colonic mucosa and in colorectal polyps and cancer is different from that in other organs, (2) the expression pattern of claudins in normal colonic epithelium is not uniform, and (3) the expression of these claudins is altered in colorectal cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of claudins in the colon and rectum.
the expression of claudin 1, 3 and 4 in the colorectal cancer and adenomas.
the study of claudin proteins (1, 3 and 4), which are involved in the regulation of the permeability of epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
claudin expression in colorectal cancer is not only a marker of differentiation but also an indicator of the prognosis.
claudin-3 and claudin-4 expression are associated with the malignant transformation of colorectal adenoma to colorectal adenocarcinoma.
the expression of claudin 1, 3 and 4 in CRC and polyps is not a reliable marker for malignancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the claudin expression profile in colorectal cancer (CRC) and polyps was different.
the expression of claudins is altered in colorectal cancer.
claudin-3, claudin-4, and claudin-5 are expressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and polyps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
claudin-4 is a marker that can help differentiate benign polyps from colorectal cancer, while claudin-3 can help differentiate benign from malignant colorectal lesions.
claudin-4, but not claudin-3, is a marker of colorectal cancer and adenomatous polyps.

we have shown that the expression of claudin 1, 3 and 4 is associated with the histological type and grade of colorectal cancer and adenomas, and that the expression of the three claudins is associated with the presence of lymph node metastases.
